soccer-ball.definition: A round ball used for playing soccer.

basketball.definition: A game played on a court by two opposing teams of 5 players.

tennis-ball.definition: A small ball used in tennis.

baseball.definition: A ball game played with a bat and ball between two teams of nine players.

volleyball.definition: A game in which two teams hit an inflated ball over a high net using their hands.

golf-ball.definition: A small, solid ball covered with dimples is struck with a club during golf, with its surface pattern helping it move through the air against less wind resistance.

rugby-ball.definition: An air-filled ball with an elongated oval shape, designed for playing rugby.

cricket-ball.definition: The specially made ball used by players in the sport of cricket.

bowling-ball.definition: A heavy round ball with finger holes, used in the sport of bowling.
bowling-ball.exampleUsage: The bowling ball rolled down the lane toward the pins.

ping-pong-ball.definition: A small lightweight hollow ball used in table tennis.
ping-pong-ball.exampleUsage: The ping-pong ball bounced once on each side of the table.

tennis-racket.definition: A handheld frame with a taut stringed surface, used to strike a tennis ball.

badminton-racket.definition: A lightweight racket with an extended handle, designed for striking a shuttlecock during badminton play.

baseball-bat.definition: A smooth club-shaped piece of sports equipment used to hit a baseball.
baseball-bat.exampleUsage: The player held the baseball bat near the handle.

cricket-bat.definition: A flat-faced wooden implement used by a cricket player to strike the ball.

hockey-stick.definition: A piece of hockey equipment with a shaped blade, used to control and move the puck across the playing surface.

golf-club.definition: A piece of sporting equipment designed to strike a golf ball during play.

lacrosse-stick.definition: A sports stick with a netted pocket at one end, used to catch, carry, and pass a lacrosse ball.
lacrosse-stick.exampleUsage: The player caught the ball in the lacrosse stick.

table-tennis-paddle.definition: A small solid racket used to hit the ball in table tennis.
table-tennis-paddle.exampleUsage: She held the table-tennis paddle ready for the serve.

squash-racket.definition: A lightweight racket with an extended handle, designed for striking the ball in squash.

polo-mallet.definition: A long-handled club that a polo player swings to strike the ball.

helmet.definition: A hard covering worn to protect the head.

shin-guards.definition: Protective pads worn over the front of the lower legs during some sports.
shin-guards.exampleUsage: The football player wore shin guards under the socks.

knee-pads.definition: Protective pads worn over the knees to reduce impact and friction.
knee-pads.exampleUsage: The skater checked that the knee pads were secure.

elbow-pads.definition: Protective pads worn over the elbows to reduce injury from falls or impacts.
elbow-pads.exampleUsage: The cyclist wore elbow pads during practice.

mouthguard.definition: A protective device worn over the teeth and gums during contact or impact sports.
mouthguard.exampleUsage: The athlete wore a fitted mouthguard during the match.

goggles.definition: (plural) tight-fitting spectacles worn to protect the eyes.

gloves.definition: The handwear used by fielders in playing baseball.

chest-protector.definition: Protective padding worn over the chest by baseball catchers and football players absorbs blows during play.

athletic-cup.definition: A protective sports item worn to shield the groin during activities with a risk of impact.
athletic-cup.exampleUsage: The equipment list includes an athletic cup for appropriate protective use.

wrist-guard.definition: A protective support worn around the wrist to reduce injury during certain sports.
wrist-guard.exampleUsage: The skater wore a wrist guard on each hand.

dumbbell.definition: A short bar with a weight at each end, used for exercise.

barbell.definition: A bar to which heavy discs are attached at each end.

resistance-band.definition: An elastic exercise band that provides resistance when stretched.
resistance-band.exampleUsage: The resistance band was used for a supervised warm-up exercise.

jump-rope.definition: A toy with a rope that is swung under the feet.

yoga-mat.definition: A soft mat used during yoga exercises.

kettlebell.definition: A heavy exercise weight shaped like a ball with a handle on top.
kettlebell.exampleUsage: The coach demonstrated safe form before the kettlebell exercise.

medicine-ball.definition: A heavy, weighted ball used to build strength and improve physical fitness.

foam-roller.definition: A firm foam cylinder used for exercise, stretching, or gentle self-massage.
foam-roller.exampleUsage: The athlete used a foam roller during the cool-down.

pull-up-bar.definition: A horizontal bar designed to support body-weight pulling exercises.
pull-up-bar.exampleUsage: The gym has a pull-up bar fixed securely to the frame.

exercise-bike.definition: A fitness machine with bicycle pedals and a fixed frame for riding indoors.
exercise-bike.exampleUsage: The exercise bike was used during the activity.

net.definition: A net stretched across a court or between players.

goal.definition: A frame or net where players score points.

hoop.definition: A circular ring used for throwing or shooting a ball.

whistle.definition: A small object blown to make a loud signal.

stopwatch.definition: A watch that measures how long an activity takes.

scoreboard.definition: A large board for displaying the score of a contest (and some other information).

cones.definition: Small pointed markers used to set out a sports course or drill.

lane-markers.definition: Lines, ropes, cones, or other markers used to divide or identify lanes in a sports area.
lane-markers.exampleUsage: Lane markers separated the swimming lanes.

starting-block.definition: Describes equipment or actions associated with starting a track race from a starting block.

hurdle.definition: An obstacle that a runner jumps over in a race.
